- Model consistently underestimates price spikes, especially after sentiment shifts to bullish (≥0.67) — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for such periods.
- After sharp price surges (e.g., >70), model fails to capture mean reversion; add a downward correction of 2–5% in next 5–7 days if sentiment turns neutral or bearish.
- When sentiment is uniformly low (≤0.33) over 3+ days, model overcorrects downward — increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model is 2–4% below true price for 10–15 days post-event — apply a 1–2% upward bias for first 10 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 1.00 entries (strong bullish), model tends to over-forecast — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 days after peak sentiment.
- Model ignores sentiment volatility — if sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00), adjust forecast mid-horizon to reflect volatility, especially in 10–15 day window.
